docs.title: Colour and monochrome
docs.text:
A NeoTrellis grid with my firmware shows colour. A monome grid shows 16 brightness levels of one colour. A script can work on both: it draws in colour where colour exists, and falls back to brightness levels where it doesn't.

color_fallback_demo.lua on a NeoTrellis grid.

docs.title: The functions
docs.text:
Function NeoTrellis firmware Monome grid (iii) grid_led(x, y, level), grid_led_all(level) Yes, in the current tint Yes grid_color(r, g, b) Sets the tint for grid_led and grid_led_all Doesn't exist grid_led_rgb(x, y, r, g, b) Sets one pad's colour, ignoring the tint Doesn't exist grid_color_intensity(level) Overall brightness Doesn't exist

On a monome grid, calling a function that doesn't exist stops the script with an error. Check first:

if grid_color then grid_color(255, 120, 20) end

To test your script without colour, pick ◐ View → Monochrome in the emulator: the colour functions disappear, as on a monome grid, and a missing check shows up as an error. On hardware, viii does the same, since it only has grid_led.

color_fallback_demo.lua on the NeoTrellis grid after testing its monochrome version in viii.

docs.title: Three ways to use colour
docs.text: Approach Use it for On a monome grid grid_color + grid_led One colour for the whole grid Same brightness levels, without the colour spx helper (below) Several colours, with a fallback Each colour becomes a brightness level grid_led_rgb only Colour that only makes sense on RGB Nothing lights up

docs.title: One colour for the whole grid
docs.text:
Set the tint once and draw as you would in monochrome:

if grid_color then grid_color(255, 120, 20) end -- amber

grid_led(1, 1, 15) -- bright amber
grid_led(2, 1, 8)  -- mid amber
grid_refresh()

The default tint is white. On my firmware, people can also pick a default tint at startup (see Getting started). Scripts that set their own colours aren't affected by it.

docs.title: Several colours, with a fallback
docs.text:
Draw every pad through one helper. On a NeoTrellis grid it sets the colour; elsewhere it turns the brightest channel into a level from 4 to 15:

local W, H = grid_size_x(), grid_size_y()

local function spx(x, y, r, g, b)
  if x < 1 or x > W or y < 1 or y > H then return end
  if grid_led_rgb then
    grid_led_rgb(x, y, r, g, b)
  else
    -- Levels 1–3 can't be seen on NeoTrellis LEDs and are very dim on monome
    -- grids, so anything that isn't black gets at least level 4.
    local level = math.floor(math.max(r, g, b) / 17)
    if level < 4 and (r > 0 or g > 0 or b > 0) then level = 4 end
    grid_led(x, y, level)
  end
end

spx(1, 1, 255, 80, 20) -- orange, or level 15
spx(2, 1, 20, 100, 255) -- blue, or level 15
spx(3, 1, 0, 40, 0)    -- dark green, or level 4

The contrast between your colours becomes the contrast between brightness levels. Full example: color_fallback_demo.lua.

docs.title: Dim colours on NeoTrellis
docs.text:
Each NeoTrellis pad mixes red, green and blue LEDs. At low brightness, the weaker channels drop out before the others, so a tinted colour can change hue. Orange (lots of red, some green) turns red when the green fades out first. Measured with grid_led and a tint:

Level What you see 1–2 Nothing 3 First visible level; the colour may be off 4–7 Visible, but cyan and blue tints can look orange or red 8–15 Accurate colour

grid_led_rgb keeps its colour better at low brightness.

color-threshold-test.lua: tinted grid_led on the left, grid_led_rgb on the right.

The emulator doesn't show these shifts. What helps:

  • Keep tinted pads at level 8 or higher.
  • For dim colours, use grid_led_rgb and keep every channel you need above about 20.
  • Use level 0 for off, and at least level 4 for on.

The thresholds can vary between NeoTrellis boards. To check yours, run color-threshold-test.lua. color-workaround-demo.lua shows the grid_led_rgb workaround.

docs.title: Developer guide
docs.text: How the emulator works inside, for changing or extending it. To write scripts instead, start with Start a script.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
index.html               The whole interface: grid, toolbar, side panel, sound, MIDI
serve.js                 Development server, and live reload over a WebSocket
engine/
  grid-api.js            Grid, LEDs, MIDI and metro timing (the "hardware")
  sound.js               Everything that plays: synth parts, drum kit, reverb, delay, chorus
  synth.js               The synth models (one voice's oscillators and filter; Karplus–Strong strings)
  drums.js               The drum kit: seven synthesised drums (from the Mangler in WAV.builder)
  lua-loader.js          Runs a script in Fengari and gives it the iii functions
  iii-lib.js             Parts of iii's lib.lua, run before every script
  doc-extractor.js       Reads the script's comments for the Docs tab and Live Manual
  script-importer.js     Fetches a script and README from GitHub or Codeberg
  lua-minifier.js        ↓ Device: strips comments, checks for code Lua 5.5 refuses
scripts/
  manifest.json          The bundled scripts in the script list
  external.json          Scripts by others: names and repository links only
  template/              Starting point for new scripts
docs/, mkdocs.yml        This documentation site

There is no build step. The page loads Fengari (Lua 5.3 in JavaScript) and marked from a CDN.

docs.title: How a script runs
docs.text:
LuaLoader._execute(source, name, dir) in lua-loader.js:

  1. Resets the grid and stops all metros and notes.
  2. Creates a new Lua state and opens the standard libraries.
  3. Adds the iii functions: grid_*, midi_*, metro, fs_*, pset_*, get_time and more. Most are small wrappers around MonomeAPI in grid-api.js.
  4. Runs iii-lib.js: the parts of the firmware's lib.lua the emulator doesn't implement in JavaScript, such as midi_out and slew. They're copied unchanged from the firmware.
  5. Runs the script.
  6. Connects pad presses to event_grid and incoming MIDI to event_midi. Both are looked up on every call, as on the device, so a script can define or replace them later.

Errors in metro ticks and events are reported once per message, and the error is taken off the Lua stack. Otherwise every later call fails as well.

dir is the script's folder (a URL). fs_run_file and require look there for files that aren't bundled scripts.

docs.title: Matching the device
docs.text:
The real API is in the firmware repo, neotrellis-monome, under neotrellis_monome_picosdk_iii/src/:

  • iii/lua/lib.lua: metro, MIDI helpers, pset, slew
  • iii/vm.c: built-ins such as midi_tx, get_time and fs_*
  • device_lua.c: grid functions

When you add or change a function, match what these do, including argument order and integer or float results. Where the emulator can't match the device, add it to Hardware vs. emulator.

docs.title: Adding a function
docs.text:
Implement it in grid-api.js and register it in lua-loader.js, next to the others:

// lua-loader.js, in _execute()
setGlobal('my_fn', (L2) => {
  lua.lua_pushinteger(L2, api.my_fn(getInt(L2, 1)));
  return 1; // number of values returned to Lua
});

// grid-api.js
my_fn(value) {
  return value * 2;
}

If the function is easier to write in Lua and the firmware has it in lib.lua, copy it into iii-lib.js instead.

docs.title: Live reload
docs.text:
serve.js serves the folder on port 3141 and watches scripts/ and its subfolders. When a .lua file changes, it sends its path (such as leaveseqr/leaveseqr.lua) over the WebSocket at /ws. If that script is running, the emulator loads it again.

npm start            # port 3141
node serve.js 8080   # another port

docs.title: Testing without a browser
docs.text:
The engine runs in Node with the fengari npm package, which is useful to check that scripts still run after an engine change:

import { createRequire } from 'module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
globalThis.window = { fengari: require('fengari') };
const store = new Map();
globalThis.localStorage = { getItem: k => store.get(k) ?? null, setItem: (k, v) => store.set(k, String(v)), removeItem: k => store.delete(k) };

const { MonomeAPI } = await import('./engine/grid-api.js');
const { LuaLoader } = await import('./engine/lua-loader.js');

const api = new MonomeAPI({ cols: 16, rows: 8 });
let notes = 0;
api.midi_note_on = () => notes++;   // the synth needs Web Audio, which Node doesn't have
api.midi_note_off = () => {};
const loader = new LuaLoader({ api, onScriptError: e => console.error(e) });

await loader._execute(source, 'myscript.lua');
api.handlePadEvent(1, 1, 1);         // press a pad

Run every script in scripts/manifest.json this way after changing the engine. Node on Windows can't time metros faster than about 15 ms, so check timing and sound in the browser.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is built with MkDocs and the Material theme. Several pages include files from elsewhere in the repo (the README, the script standard, script READMEs) with include-markdown, so each text exists once.

pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin
mkdocs serve

docs/index.md is also shown in the emulator's About dialog, so keep it plain Markdown (no include-markdown).

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
Every push to main publishes the site through .github/workflows/deploy.yml:

  1. It builds this documentation into docs/ of the site.
  2. It copies the emulator (index.html, engine/, scripts/ and so on) next to it, and the raw docs/ folder as emulator-docs/ for the About dialog.
  3. It pushes the result to the gh-pages branch, which GitHub Pages serves.

So the emulator is at /diii-neotrellis-emulator/ and the documentation at /diii-neotrellis-emulator/docs/. In a fork, set Settings → Pages → Source to the gh-pages branch after the first run.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: There are three ways in: play scripts in the browser, run the emulator on your own computer to write scripts, or put scripts on a NeoTrellis grid.

docs.title: Use it in the browser
docs.text:
1. Open the emulator: jonwaterschoot.github.io/diii-neotrellis-emulator.
  2. Pick a script from the list and press ▶ Load.
  3. Click the grid. The sound starts muted, and the first click unmutes it.

To send MIDI to a synth or DAW, pick a MIDI output in the toolbar. That needs a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge). The walkthrough explains the rest of the screen.

docs.title: Run it on your computer
docs.text:
Running the emulator locally lets you edit scripts in your own editor: when you save a .lua file in scripts/, the emulator reloads it.

You need Node.js.

git clone https://github.com/jonwaterschoot/diii-neotrellis-emulator.git
cd diii-neotrellis-emulator
npm install
npm start

Then open http://localhost:3141.

To write your own script, pick Write your own → Script template in the script list, or read Start a script.

docs.title: Put scripts on a NeoTrellis grid
docs.text: The grid runs my fork of okyeron's neotrellis-monome firmware, with monome's iii scripting and colour support added: jonwaterschoot/neotrellis-monome.

docs.title: Install the firmware
docs.text:
1. Download a .uf2 file from the latest firmware release. neotrellis-iii-pico-128-…uf2 is for a Pico with a 16×8 grid. The release also has 8×8, 4×4 and dink-ii builds, which haven't been tested on hardware.
  2. Hold the BOOTSEL button on the Pico while plugging it in. It shows up as a drive.
  3. Drag the .uf2 file onto that drive. The Pico restarts with the new firmware.

To build the firmware yourself, or for other boards and grid sizes, see the firmware README.

docs.title: Startup options
docs.text:
• Mode: hold the top-left button while powering on to switch modes. One lit pixel means serial mode (monome/norns apps); three lit pixels across the top row mean iii mode (diii scripts).
  • Colour: hold the top-right button while powering on to pick the colour that tints monochrome scripts. Press a colour, then the top-right button to save it. Scripts that set their own colours aren't affected.

Hold both buttons to do both in one go.

docs.title: Upload scripts
docs.text:
Upload .lua files with the diii web app (Chrome).

  • Before uploading, read Hardware vs. emulator, and download the script with ↓ Device: it strips comments and warns about code the device won't load.
  • Restart the grid before uploading, or at least stop a busy script: an upload while a heavy script runs can fail.
  • To choose a script at startup, use selector (also on the release page). Every script on the grid gets a coloured slot: press it once to see the name, again to start it. Make selector the startup script with first("selector.lua") in the diii console.

docs.title: If the grid won't start
docs.text:
A script that crashes at startup can lock you out. To recover:

  • Start in serial mode and open the viii web app: it can reformat the storage and enter the bootloader.
  • Or flash the Raspberry Pi flash nuke UF2, which erases everything, then install the firmware again.

docs.title: Hardware vs. emulator
docs.text: The emulator runs your Lua script in the browser. On a grid, the same script runs on the Pico with the iii firmware. Most scripts behave the same in both places. This page lists where they don't, so that a script that works in the emulator also works on the device.

docs.title: Before you upload
docs.text:
• Download the script with ↓ Device. It strips comments to make the file smaller, and the status bar warns about code the device won't load.
  • Use at most 11 metros. The status bar warns when a script uses more.
  • Call emulator-only functions behind a check, such as if grid_set_screen then.
  • Call midi_note_off(note, vel, ch) with all three arguments.
  • Free a metro with metro.free(m.id), not metro.free(m).
  • Don't count on fs_write_file: the emulator's files are read-only.

docs.title: Lua version
docs.text:
Device Emulator Lua 5.5 5.3 (Fengari)
  • Read-only loop variables. Lua 5.5 doesn't let a script assign to a for loop variable. for i = 1, 8 do i = i + 1 end runs in the emulator, but the device won't load the script. Copy the variable instead: local j = i. ↓ Device warns about these assignments.
  • Newer features. local x <const> = 1 and <close> come from Lua 5.4: the device runs them, the emulator gives a parse error. warn() is also 5.4: in the emulator it doesn't exist.
  • Integers. Grid coordinates in event_grid, grid_size_x() and grid_size_y() are integers in both, so x .. "" gives "1", not "1.0".

docs.title: Memory and script size
docs.text:
The device has little memory. A large script can run out of memory while uploading or while running. The emulator has no memory limit and can't measure memory use:

  • collectgarbage("count") returns 0.
  • collectgarbage("step") returns false.
  • The other collectgarbage options do nothing.

A script that runs in the emulator can still be too big for the device. Stock iii can't upload scripts larger than about 32 KB; my firmware fork fixes that. ↓ Device makes a smaller copy without comments.

docs.title: Metros
docs.text:
Device Emulator Metros 12; slew takes one at boot, so a script gets 11 No limit; the status bar warns past 12 (counting slew's) When none is left metro.init returns nil and prints metro.init: nothing available Keeps working Timing Hardware timers Browser timers
  • metro.free takes the metro's number: metro.free(m.id). Passing the metro itself, metro.free(m), is an error on the device, and the emulator raises the same error.
  • metro.free_all() also stops slew's metro, on both.
  • Normal tempos keep time in the browser. Very short periods (a few milliseconds) depend on the browser. A tab in the background is slowed down; the emulator then skips ticks instead of playing the missed ones all at once.

docs.title: MIDI
docs.text:
Both have midi_note_on, midi_note_off, midi_cc, midi_tx, midi_out and event_midi.

Device Emulator MIDI out USB MIDI to the connected computer The MIDI output picked in the toolbar (Web MIDI, Chromium-based browsers), plus a built-in synth MIDI in event_midi(d1, d2, d3) event_midi too. A script without event_midi gets incoming notes as pad presses (emulator only) CC 74 Sent as a CC Also moves the emulator's filter
  • Note-offs. Use midi_note_off(note, vel, ch). The emulator still accepts the old two-argument form midi_note_off(note, ch). On the device the second argument is the velocity, so those note-offs go to channel 1.
  • Echo. If the emulator's MIDI input and output are the same device, a script hears its own output, such as its own clock. The status bar warns when that happens.

docs.title: Files and presets
docs.text:
The device has a small file system. The emulator has a read-only stand-in:

Function Device Emulator fs_list_files() Files on the device The bundled scripts, by file name fs_run_file(name), require(name) Runs a file Runs a bundled script, or a file next to the running script fs_read_file(name) Reads a file Reads the same files fs_write_file, fs_remove_file, fs_file_size, fs_free_space, fs_reformat Yes Not available pset_init, pset_write, pset_read, pset_delete pset_*.lua files Browser storage

Because presets live in browser storage, they don't show up in fs_list_files(), and presets saved in one browser aren't in another.

The REPL helpers from iii's lib.lua (first, ls, rm, cat, mem, gc) don't exist in the emulator. Use them from the diii console.

docs.title: Grid and LEDs
docs.text:
Functions Where grid_led (with rel), grid_led_all (with rel), grid_led_get, grid_refresh, grid_size_x, grid_size_y, grid_intensity Device and emulator grid_led_rgb, grid_color, grid_color_intensity NeoTrellis firmware and emulator. Not on a monochrome monome grid: check if grid_led_rgb then (monochrome fallback). ◐ View → Monochrome hides them in the emulator, to test that grid_set_screen, display_screen, get_focused_screen, grid_brightness Emulator only (multiple screens) event_key(key) Emulator only: the device has no keyboard, so it never calls it
  • Size and rotation. A device's grid size is fixed. In the emulator you pick it in the toolbar, or a script's manifest sets it. grid_size_x() and grid_size_y() report the chosen size.
  • Colours. The emulator brightens dim LEDs to look like real ones, but it doesn't copy the NeoTrellis colour shifts at low brightness. See Colour and monochrome.

docs.title: Errors, printing and time
docs.text:
Device Emulator print The diii console The browser's developer console (F12), not the Console tab Errors Printed in the diii console Each different error shows once in the status bar and the Console tab; the Source tab marks its line get_time() Seconds since the device started Seconds since the script was loaded

Use get_time() to measure time between events, not as a clock.

docs.title: Only in the emulator
docs.text:
• The keyboard: R reloads the script. A script with event_key gets the other keys; for other scripts, some keys press fixed pads. See keyboard shortcuts.
  • The built-in synth, the effects and the filter play what the script sends as MIDI. The device only sends MIDI.

docs.title: LeaveSeqr
docs.text:
Ambient leaf physics sequencer for Neotrellis grids: leaves drift through the air, float on the water surface, and sink slowly to the mud. Three independent generative water tracks play notes as leaves pass over the playheads. Triops leap into the water to eat the sinking leaves, causing a bouncing bass echo delay.

  • Author: jonwaterschoot
  • Version: v0.3.1

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Navigate the grid using three screens. Hold ALT (x=1, y=3) to cycle between the screens: Live (physics simulation), Seq (sequencer settings), and Scale (musical settings). By default, the sequencer runs at full 16 steps and runs at different relative speeds from top to bottom (surface is fastest, mid is slower, deep is the slowest).

docs.title: Main Controls (Present on all screens)
docs.text: Location Label Description x=1, y=8 ALT Cycle screens: Live → Seq → Scale x=1, y=3 Play/Stop Play/stop sequencer & physics (Live only) x=16, y=3 Freeze Pause leaves in water zones (Live only)

docs.title: Screen 1: Live Simulation (Default)
docs.text:
The primary view where the ambient ecosystem lives.

  • Row 1 (Canopy): Leaves grow here. Tap a leaf to knock it loose, or tap an empty spot to plant.
  • Row 2 (Wind):
  • x=1..3: Left wind — gusts push leaves horizontally to the right, and blows canopy loose.
  • x=14..16: Right wind — gusts push leaves horizontally to the left, and blows canopy loose.
  • Row 2..4 (Air Zone): Leaves drift slowly down. Wind pushes horizontally and sometimes upward.
  • Row 5 (Water Surface): Track 1, plays at base octave limit.
  • Row 6 (Underwater Mid): Track 2, plays one octave down.
  • Row 7 (Underwater Deep): Track 3, plays two octaves down.
  • Row 8 (Mud): Leaves collect and decay at the bottom. Triops emerge occasionally.

docs.title: Screen 2: Sequencer Settings
docs.text:
Customize how the leaves trigger notes when they reach the water tracks.

Top Row (y=1) Track Options: 1. x=1 LEN — tap a track row twice to set loop start and end bounds (left-to-right is forward, right-to-left is reverse). 2. x=2 DIV — tap x=1..6 on a track row to set track division (playback speed). 3. x=3 CH — tap x=1..16 on a track row to set MIDI channel. 4. x=4 OCT — tap x=1..8 on a track row to set octave offset bounds (-4 to +3).

Row 2-4 Controls: - BPM: x=1..4, y=2 (-10, -1, +1, +10) - Wind Str: x=1..3, y=3 (lo, mid, hi) - Density: x=5..8, y=3 (off, lo, mid, hi) - Humanize: x=1..3, y=4 (off, soft, heavy) - Triops: x=5, y=4 (off, soft, strong)

Tracks: Modify the tracks by tapping at their live y positions (Rows 5, 6, 7).

docs.title: Screen 3: Scale & Environment
docs.text:
Tune the harmony, environment, and physical appearance.

Component Location Controls Description Scale Modes x=1..7, y=1 Labeled: MAJ, MIN, PMA, PMI, DOR, LYD, CUS Black Keys x=1,2,4,5,6, y=3 Labeled: C#, D#, F#, G#, A# (aligned to grid) White Keys x=1..7, y=4 Labeled: C, D, E, F, G, A, B Octave Base x=1..4, y=6 Labeled: OC2, OC3, OC4, OC5 Season x=1..4, y=7 Labeled: SPR, SUM, AUT, WIN Monochrome x=6, y=7 Toggle monochrome mode on/off

docs.title: Seasons
docs.text:
Seasons change leaf colors, note character, and MIDI CC filter automation simultaneously.

Season Colors Notes MIDI CC SP Spring Bright greens Short, energetic · high velocity Neutral (CC 100) SU Summer Warm yellow-greens Long, sustained · high velocity Neutral (CC 100) AU Autumn Warm oranges & reds Short–medium · velocity variance · 25% chord chance (third or fifth) Slow, wide filter sweeps WI Winter Cool blues & greys Long and short mixed · lower velocity · 15% echo chance Fast, jittery filter drift

Spring and Summer leave the MIDI CC filter at 100 (fully open, no movement). Autumn and Winter drive a slow-moving CC ramp on CC 74 — Autumn sweeps broadly and slowly, Winter drifts fast and erratically. If your synth or DAW responds to CC 74 (filter cutoff), these seasons will animate the filter automatically. | Grid Dimming | x=3..5, y=8 | Grid brightness levels: lo, mid, max | | ALT | x=1, y=8 | Momentary: exit settings; Double-tap: sticky mode |

docs.title: diii-neotrellis-emulator
docs.text:
A browser emulator for monome iii grid scripts. It runs the same Lua scripts as a NeoTrellis or monome grid, plays them through a built-in synth or MIDI, and shows each script's controls on the grid as a live manual.

Open the emulator · Documentation

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Play scripts: the bundled ones, scripts by others (loaded from their own repositories), any GitHub or Codeberg repository, or a file from your computer.
  • Hear them: several synths at once (from soft keys to Karplus–Strong strings) and a drum kit, with reverb, delay and chorus; MIDI out to a synth or DAW, and MIDI in for scripts that follow a clock or a keyboard.
  • Read them: each script's controls are drawn over the grid, its README shows in the Guide tab and its code in the Source tab.
  • Write them: edit and run a script in the browser, or in your own editor with live reload. ↓ Device makes a smaller copy for uploading and warns about code the device won't load.
  • See them your way: NeoTrellis pads or Mechatrellis keys, dark or light, in colour or as a monochrome monome grid.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
• Use it in the browser, nothing to install.
  • Run it on your computer to write scripts: npm install, then npm start.
  • Put scripts on a NeoTrellis grid: the firmware is on the firmware release page.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
My scripts, as grouped in the emulator's script list:

  • Music: LeaveSeqr (falling leaves become three sequencer tracks), Sandman (falling sand, leaves and water as music), Serpentine (a snake game sequencer).
  • Colour demos: colour fallback demo, monochrome fallback, colour workaround demo, text runner.
  • Tests: multiple screens, grid colour, colour threshold, power.
  • Write your own: the script template, with a step-by-step guide and instructions to give an LLM.

docs.title: Scripts by others
docs.text:
The emulator's script list also offers scripts by other people. They are not my work and they are not part of this project or copied into this repo: scripts/external.json only holds their names and repository links, and the emulator fetches each script from its author's repository when you load it. All credit goes to the authors.

If you wrote one of these and would rather not be listed, please open an issue and I'll take it out.

  • kria iii by aktsom
  • stepiii by nolliegray
  • arpiii by nolliegray
  • fugace by behindkeyframes
  • iiinvert by liamelliot
  • fell by liamelliot

docs.title: Sandman
docs.text:
A living portrait of falling sand, leaves and water that turn into music.

Mount your NeoTrellis rotated 90° counterclockwise (power cable at top). The grid becomes 8 columns × 16 rows in portrait. Grains accumulate at the bottom and become a step sequencer.

  • Author: jonwaterschoot
  • Version: v0.1.2
  • Forum: (link pending)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Boot the script. The top row fills with random grains (reservoir).
  2. Tap one of the four drop-zone pads (portrait col 3-6, row 2) to release a grain — it falls and piles up.
  3. Hold a drop-zone pad for 0.4 s then release to stream up to 16 grains automatically.
  4. Tap left or right half of the reservoir row to shift it left or right; new grains appear on the far side.
  5. Press Start/Stop to start the sequencer. Grains that have settled in the bottom 8 rows (portrait rows 9-16) become playable steps.
  6. Tap settled grains to mine them (3 taps clears a grain, freeing space above).
  7. Enable Lock to freeze physics — grains stop dissolving and the settled area plays like a normal pad grid.

docs.title: Script Documentation Standard
docs.text: This document defines the standard for how scripts are documented in this emulator. It is intentionally kept close to the norns/monome ecosystem conventions so that community scripts can be imported with minimal adaptation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A script is a single .lua file, or a folder with the .lua file and more. The emulator reads its documentation from three places:

Source Used for Comments in the .lua file The Docs tab, the Live Manual overlay and the keyboard hints (sections 1, 2, 6 and 7) README.md next to the .lua file The Guide tab (section 3) manifest.json in the folder Which .lua file to load and where the README is, when importing from a repository (section 4)

A script doesn't need all three. A .lua file with good comments works on its own; a repository with the .lua file and a README.md is the recommended minimum.

docs.title: 1. Lua file header (required)
docs.text:
The top of every script should have an uninterrupted block of -- comments:

-- scriptname: Human Readable Script Name
-- v1.0.0
-- @author: Your Name
-- llllllll.co/t/your-thread  (or any URL)
--
-- One-line description of what the script does.

Rules: - First line: -- scriptname: Name (parsed by doc-extractor.js) - Second line: -- vX.Y.Z (semver, parsed as version) - @author line is optional but encouraged - A bare URL on its own line is parsed as the discussion/reference link - The first untagged line after scriptname becomes the short description - The header ends at the first non-comment line - Optional: -- @orientation portrait (or portrait-cw, portrait-ccw) in the first 30 lines rotates the grid when the script loads, for scripts meant to be played with the grid turned 90°

This mirrors the norns script header convention used in the community catalog.

docs.title: 2. Inline control map comments (for the grid overlay)
docs.text:
Inside the script, use -- comments in the following format to describe grid positions. These are extracted by doc-extractor.js and rendered as the map overlay.

-- x=1, y=8: ALT toggle — momentary press opens Settings, double-tap = sticky
-- x=1..8, y=1: Spawn quantity slider (2 fruits per step, max 16)
-- Row 3, x=1: Autopilot mode cycles NON → SEM → AUT
-- Row 6, col 2..7: Black keys — C# D# F# G# A# (skips the gap)

Supported location formats (all case-insensitive): - x=N — single column - x=N..M — column range - y=N — single row (as row number) - x=N, y=M — specific cell - Row N — entire row - Row N, col M — specific cell by row/col - Cols N-M / Col N — column range or single col

A control comment must end with : description — the colon is the delimiter.

docs.title: Sections, groups, and screen assignment
docs.text:
The hierarchy is: Section → Group → Control

-- @section Section Name    ← major logical block; resets @screen and @group
-- @screen live             ← all controls below go to the main (primary) grid
-- @screen settings         ← named alt screen — shown in the ghost grid beside main
-- @screen menu             ← another named alt screen — gets its own tab in the ghost grid

-- @group Group Name        ← start a named group; controls below belong to it
-- @detail First line of extended description for this group.
-- @detail Additional lines accumulate — each @detail line appends to the previous.
-- x=N, y=M: Description   ← sub-control inside the group
-- x=N, y=M: Description
-- @group                   ← empty @group clears the group; next controls are singletons
-- x=N, y=M: Description   ← singleton — gets its own overlay card

@detail text attaches an extended description to the group declared immediately above it. Multiple consecutive @detail lines are concatenated with a newline, so you can write multi-line explanations. The detail is cleared whenever a new @group or @section tag is encountered, so each group gets its own isolated annotation. The detail is surfaced in the live manual panel in the emulator as supplementary copy below the group's control list.

-- @group Water Tracks
-- @detail Each row is an independent sequencer track with its own playhead.
-- @detail When a leaf sits on a playhead position, it triggers a note.
-- @detail Track length, speed, MIDI channel, and octave are set on the Seq screen.
-- Row 5: TR1 — Water surface, base octave
-- Row 6: TR2 — Underwater mid, one octave down
-- Row 7: TR3 — Underwater deep, two octaves down

docs.title: Best Practices for Layout and Ordering
1. Range Prefixing and Labels
docs.text: When documenting a range of pads (e.g., x=1..4), you can include a descriptive "prefix" followed by a separator like an em-dash (—) or colon (:). The renderer ignores this prefix when calculating how many words match the pad count. - Good: -- x=1..4, y=7: SEAS — SPR SUM AUT WIN (4 labels for 4 pads; prefix ignored) - Bad: -- x=1..4, y=7: SEAS SPR SUM AUT WIN (5 words for 4 pads; labels may break)

docs.title: 2. The Capture Rule for @detail
docs.text: To ensure that the sidebar "live manual" captures the full description, always place the coordinate mapping line at the bottom of the group block. - Correct Ordering: lua -- @group Themes -- @detail Each season changes the color and character of the notes. -- x=1..4, y=7: SEAS — SPR SUM AUT WIN

docs.title: 3. Handling Gaps (Piano Layouts)
docs.text:
For non-contiguous controls (like piano black keys), use split ranges instead of placeholders to ensure perfect physical alignment:

-- x=2..3, y=3: BLACK — C# D#
-- x=5..7, y=3: BLACK — F# G# A#

@section defines a major logical grouping (e.g. "Grid Layout", "Settings View"). Resets both @screen and @group.

@screen <name> sets which visual grid this section/group renders on in the map overlay.

Naming convention: - live — always the primary/main screen. This name is fixed and expected by the emulator. It is the only screen shown in single-view by default and always occupies the main grid in dual-view. - Any other name becomes a secondary screen — shown in the ghost grid (dual-view) or swapped in as the main view (single-view). Use short, descriptive lowercase words: settings, menu, edit1, page2, etc. Scripts with multiple secondary screens get a tab row in dual-view so the user can switch between them.

The name is used as the ghost grid label and in the minimap. Persists until the next @section or another @screen tag.

@group Name starts a named group. All controls until the next @group, @group (empty, to close), or @section belong to this group. In the overlay, the group renders as one card with a fan of bezier lines to each sub-control's pad position. An empty -- @group closes the group — subsequent controls become singletons again.

Full-grid controls (x=1..16, y=1..8) are automatically excluded from the overlay since they describe the whole grid rather than a specific interaction point.

docs.title: Multi-screen rendering (required pattern for dual-view and minimap)
docs.text:
The emulator maintains a separate frame buffer per screen name. The minimap and ghost grid (dual-view) are only populated if content is written to those buffers. A script that only ever draws to live will have empty thumbnails and an empty ghost grid.

Required approach: render ALL screens into their buffers on every redraw(), then call grid_refresh() once. grid_refresh() flushes every buffer simultaneously — the minimap, ghost grid, and main grid all update in one pass.

function redraw()
    -- Primary screen
    grid_set_screen('live')
    grid_led_all(0)
    -- ... draw live content ...

    -- Each secondary screen gets its own buffer
    grid_set_screen('settings')
    grid_led_all(0)
    -- ... draw settings content ...

    -- One flush updates everything: main grid, ghost grid, all minimap tiles
    grid_refresh()
end

grid_set_screen(name) switches which buffer subsequent grid_led / grid_led_rgb / grid_led_all calls write to. Call it before drawing each screen's content.

display_screen(name) signals the emulator which screen is currently active — this controls the minimap highlight and switches the ghost grid in dual-view. Call it whenever the user navigates between screens. Guard with if display_screen then for hardware compatibility (the function only exists in the emulator; see Hardware vs. emulator):

-- When navigating to a secondary screen:
if display_screen then display_screen('settings') end

-- When returning to main:
if display_screen then display_screen('live') end

Backwards compatibility note: with serial testing with the viii app to run scripts over serial for OG monome norns compatibility — i learned to not provide grid_set_screen. In that case, scripts should either stub it or branch around it and draw only the active screen. For example:

local supports_multi_screen = (grid_set_screen ~= nil)
if not grid_set_screen then grid_set_screen = function(name) end end

function redraw()
  if supports_multi_screen then
    grid_set_screen('live')
    -- draw live and alternate screen buffers...
    grid_set_screen('settings')
    -- draw settings screen...
  else
    -- draw only the currently active screen
  end
  grid_refresh()
end

The same compatibility pattern applies to display_screen and any alternate-screen logic.

Full example (from serpentine_dev.lua):

-- @section Grid Layout
-- @screen live
-- x=1, y=8: ALT — momentary hold opens Settings; double-tap = sticky
-- x=2, y=8: Play/Stop — green=running, red=stopped
-- @group D-PAD
-- x=15, y=7: UP
-- x=14, y=8: LEFT
-- x=15, y=8: DOWN
-- x=16, y=8: RIGHT

-- @section Settings View (hold ALT)
-- @screen settings
-- x=1..8, y=1: Spawn Quantity — slider, each step = 2 fruits
-- @group Fruit Type Toggles
-- x=11, y=1: Red — tail shrink, note to pool
-- x=12, y=1: Blue — tail grow, note to pool
-- @group
-- x=1, y=3: Autopilot — dim=manual, bright=auto
-- @group BPM Adjust
-- x=10, y=3: −10 BPM
-- x=11, y=3: −1 BPM
-- x=12, y=3: +1 BPM
-- x=13, y=3: +10 BPM
-- @group
-- @group Root Note Keyboard
-- x=1..7, y=6: Black keys (C# D# F# G# A#)
-- x=1..7, y=7: White keys (C D E F G A B)

docs.title: 3. README.md (recommended for GitHub repos)
docs.text:
A README.md in the same folder as the .lua file is the script's full manual. The emulator shows it in the Guide tab, rendered as Markdown. Relative links and images resolve against the README's own folder, so ![](../img/layout.png) works.

There's no required structure. These sections are a good order for a grid script:

## Usage       ← how to start: what to press first
## Controls    ← what each pad does, often as a table
## Settings    ← the settings or ALT screens
## Notes       ← limits, hardware notes, tips
## Changelog

The reference is scripts/serpentineSeqr/README.md.

docs.title: 4. manifest.json (optional, for importing)
docs.text:
A manifest.json in the script's folder tells the emulator which file to load when someone imports the repository. The shape follows the norns community catalog:

{
  "project_name": "serpentine",
  "project_url": "https://github.com/user/repo",
  "author": "your-name",
  "description": "Snake sequencer with arpeggiator for NeoTrellis 16x8",
  "discussion_url": "https://llllllll.co/t/your-thread/12345",
  "documentation_url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/user/repo/main/README.md",
  "tags": ["sequencer", "generative", "neotrellis", "rgb"],
  "lua_file": "myscript.lua"
}

The emulator uses two fields:

  • lua_file: the script to load. Without it, the emulator tries <repository name>.lua, then index.lua, then the first .lua file in the folder.
  • documentation_url: where the README is. Without it, the emulator uses README.md in the script's folder, then in the repository root.

The other fields describe the script for people and for future catalogs.

Scripts that come with the emulator are listed in scripts/manifest.json instead, which also sets their group in the script list, their README and their grid size: see Start a script.

docs.title: 5. Importing from GitHub or Codeberg
docs.text:
⇱ Import script repo takes a repository address: github.com/owner/repo, codeberg.org/owner/repo, or owner/repo for GitHub. A folder inside a repository works too: github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/path/to/script. The emulator:

  1. Tries the main branch, then master, unless the address names a branch.
  2. Reads manifest.json if there is one, and finds the .lua file as in section 4.
  3. Runs the script, and reads its comments for the Docs tab and Live Manual.
  4. Shows the README in the Guide tab.

Files from public GitHub and Codeberg repositories can be fetched straight from the browser, so no server is needed.

docs.title: 6. Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
In the emulator, a script can handle keys with event_key(key). It's called once per key press (not on release, and not for a held key's repeats), with the key's name: "space", "tab", "enter", "up", "down", "left", "right", or the character in lower case ("a", "1").

function event_key(key)
  if key == "tab" then next_screen() end
end

R always reloads the script and never reaches event_key. A script without event_key gets the emulator's fixed pad presses instead (Tab and Space press x1, y8, and so on; see the walkthrough). The device has no keyboard and never calls event_key, so keep every action reachable from the grid too.

docs.title: Hints (@key)
docs.text:
Scripts can declare their keyboard shortcuts using @key tags in the header block. The emulator reads these and populates the hints bar below the grid automatically. The R key (Reload) is always shown as an app-level entry at the end; do not redeclare it.

-- @key ↑↓←→: Steer
-- @key Tab: Settings
-- @key Space: Sticky
-- @key 1/2: BPM−
-- @key 3/4: BPM+
-- @key A: Autopilot

Notation rules: - Place @key lines anywhere in the leading comment block (same area as the header) - Format: -- @key KEYS: Label - KEYS is the text shown in the badge — keep it short (≤8 characters) - Use / to separate two keys that share a label: 1/2 renders as two separate badges with / between them - Unicode symbols are fine: ↑↓←→, ⌘, ⇧ - Label is plain text; keep it to 1–2 words

docs.title: 7. LDoc tag reference (what doc-extractor.js recognizes)
docs.text:
Tag Usage Example -- scriptname: Name Script name (first header line) -- scriptname: Serpentine -- @author: name Author (header) -- @author: jonwaterschoot -- @orientation o Rotate the grid on load (header, first 30 lines) -- @orientation portrait --- description Triple-dash opens a doc block --- Updates the snake position -- @tparam type name desc Typed parameter -- @tparam number x Grid column (1-16) -- @treturn type desc Typed return value (@returns also works) -- @treturn boolean True if alive -- @param name desc Untyped parameter -- @param x Column -- @section Name Groups following controls -- @section Spawner Engine -- @screen name Which screen the following controls are on -- @screen settings -- @group Name Starts a named group -- @group D-PAD -- @detail text Extended description for the current group (multi-line, accumulates) -- @detail Leaves drift slowly downward. -- @key KEYS: Label Keyboard shortcut hint -- @key ↑↓←→: Steer -- x=N: desc Control map (single cell) -- x=1, y=8: ALT toggle -- Row N: desc Control map (full row) -- Row 6: Black keys

Tags from the full LDoc spec that are not currently extracted (low priority for grid scripts): @usage, @see, @field, @release, @license, @classmod, @module, @script

These can be added to doc-extractor.js incrementally as needed.

docs.title: Serpentine Sequencer
docs.text:
A snake sequencer game for the NeoTrellis / Monome-compatible 16x8 RGB grid. The snake eats fruit to collect notes into an arpeggiator pool. Each fruit type triggers a different musical event on collection.

  • Author: jonwaterschoot (jonwtr)
  • Version: v1.3.1
  • Forum: (link pending)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Navigate the snake with the D-PAD (bottom-right corner of the grid). Hold or double-tap ALT (bottom-left) to open the Settings overlay without stopping the sequencer.

The snake eats coloured fruit. Each fruit type adds a note to the arpeggiator pool and triggers a musical side-effect. The sequencer runs continuously — ALT mode is a live overlay.

docs.text:
• The sequencer never stops when entering/exiting Settings — ALT is a live overlay

  • Monochrome mode tints are cinematic presets, not user-configurable per-tint

docs.title: How to start a new NeoTrellis script
docs.text:
This folder is a starter template. Copy it, rename things, and build from here.

Working with an LLM? Give it LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md together with myscript.lua. All template files: scripts/template/.

docs.title: Step 1 — Copy and rename the folder
docs.text:
1. Duplicate this template/ folder somewhere inside scripts/.
  2. Rename the folder to match your script (e.g. scripts/mysequencer/).
  3. Rename myscript.lua to match your script name (e.g. mysequencer.lua).
  4. Lowercase, no spaces — use underscores if needed.

docs.title: Step 2 — Edit the Lua header
docs.text:
Open your .lua file. The first block of comments is parsed by the emulator. Fill in every field:

-- scriptname: My Sequencer         ← required, shown in the UI
-- v0.1.0                           ← semver, update as you go
-- @author: Your Name               ← optional but encouraged
-- https://llllllll.co/t/...        ← your forum thread URL (add when you have one)
--
-- What the script does in one line. ← required, becomes the short description

Do not leave empty lines inside this header block. The parser stops at the first non-comment line.

docs.title: Step 3 — Keyboard shortcuts (optional, emulator only)
docs.text:
Handle keys in event_key, and list them with @key lines in the header so they show under the grid:

-- @key Tab: Next screen
-- @key Space: Play/Stop

function event_key(key)
  if key == "tab" then next_screen()
  elseif key == "space" then toggle_play() end
end

key is the key's name: "space", "tab", "enter", "up", "down", "left", "right", or the character in lower case ("a", "1"). It's called on each press, not on release. R always reloads the script.

The device has no keyboard, so make every action reachable from the grid too. Scripts without event_key get fixed pad presses instead (Tab and Space press x1, y8, the arrows press x14–16, y7–8); the script standard has the details.

docs.title: Step 4 — Map your grid controls
docs.text:
Add control-map comments before the first non-comment line of real code (or grouped under -- @section headings anywhere in the file):

-- @section Main Screen
-- @screen live
-- x=1, y=8: ALT — opens Settings
-- x=2, y=8: Play/Stop

-- @section Settings
-- @screen settings
-- x=1..8, y=1: My slider — range description

These become the interactive overlay the emulator draws over the grid.

docs.title: Adding extended descriptions with @detail
docs.text:
Place one or more -- @detail lines immediately after a @group line to attach a longer description to that group. Multiple @detail lines accumulate (newline-joined). The emulator surfaces these as supplementary copy beneath the group's control list in the live manual panel.

-- @group Water Tracks
-- @detail Each row is an independent sequencer track with its own playhead.
-- @detail When a leaf sits on a playhead position, it triggers a MIDI note.
-- @detail Track length, speed, channel, and octave are set in the Seq screen.
-- Row 5: TR1 — Water surface, base octave
-- Row 6: TR2 — Underwater mid, one octave down
-- Row 7: TR3 — Underwater deep, two octaves down

The @detail annotation is cleared whenever a new @group or @section tag is encountered, so each group gets its own description.

Best Practice for Ordering: Always place your coordinate lines (e.g. x=1..4: ...) at the bottom of the group block. This ensures the sidebar "live manual" captures all the detail text that came before it.

Best Practice for Labels: Use a prefix header for ranges (e.g. SEAS — SPR SUM AUT WIN). The emulator ignores words before the dash when mapping labels to pads, allowing for better sidebar clarity.

docs.title: Step 5 — Keep the compatibility stubs
docs.text:
The template includes these at the top of the code section:

local supports_multi_screen = (grid_set_screen ~= nil)
if not grid_set_screen  then grid_set_screen  = function(_) end end
if not display_screen   then display_screen   = function(_) end end

Leave these in place. They let your script run on real Pico hardware (where those functions don't exist) without errors.

docs.title: Step 6 — Write your redraw() and event_grid() functions
docs.text:
These are the two cores of every script:

  • redraw() — called by your clock or after any input. Always end with grid_refresh().
  • event_grid(x, y, z) — called by the hardware/emulator whenever a pad is pressed or released.

The template shows the minimal structure. Expand from there.

docs.title: Step 6b — Colour
docs.text:
A NeoTrellis grid shows colour; a monome grid shows brightness levels 0–15. The colour functions only exist on the NeoTrellis firmware (and in the emulator), so check before calling them.

One colour for the whole grid: set a tint once, then draw with grid_led as usual.

if grid_color then grid_color(255, 120, 20) end -- amber on NeoTrellis, white elsewhere
grid_led(1, 1, 15)

Several colours: draw every pad through one helper that falls back to brightness levels.

local function spx(x, y, r, g, b)
  if grid_led_rgb then
    grid_led_rgb(x, y, r, g, b)
  else
    local level = math.floor(math.max(r, g, b) / 17)
    if level < 4 and (r > 0 or g > 0 or b > 0) then level = 4 end -- 1–3 are too dim to see
    grid_led(x, y, level)
  end
end

spx(1, 1, 255, 80, 20) -- orange, or level 15 on a monome grid

Dim tinted colours can change hue on NeoTrellis hardware, which the emulator doesn't show. The details, measured thresholds and test scripts are in Colour and monochrome. Full example: color_fallback_demo.lua.

docs.title: Step 7 — Update manifest.json
docs.text:
Open manifest.json and fill in every field:

Field What to put project_name Same as folder name, lowercase project_url Your GitHub repo URL author Your display name description Same one-liner as the Lua header discussion_url llllllll.co thread (add when ready) documentation_url Raw GitHub URL to your README.md tags Relevant tags: e.g. ["sequencer", "neotrellis"] lua_file Your .lua filename

docs.title: Step 8 — Register your script in scripts/manifest.json
docs.text:
Open the top-level scripts/manifest.json and add an entry:

{
  "name": "My Sequencer",
  "group": "Music",
  "file": "mysequencer/mysequencer.lua",
  "readme": "mysequencer/README.md",
  "description": "What it does",
  "author": "Your Name",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "gridSize": [16, 8]
}

After saving, your script appears in the emulator's script list, under its group (scripts with the same group are listed together, in file order). gridSize sets the grid when it loads; add "orientation": "portrait" for a script played with the grid turned 90°.

docs.title: Step 9 — Write your README.md
docs.text: Fill in the template's README.md: it's the manual people read in the Guide tab. Usage, Controls, Settings, Notes and Changelog are a good order; the script standard has more.

docs.title: Common gotchas
docs.text:
• Always call grid_refresh() once at the end of redraw() — not after individual grid_led calls.
  • Guard display_screen() calls: if display_screen then display_screen("settings") end
  • Pico memory is limited: avoid large string tables, deep elseif chains, and anonymous function allocation inside hot loops.
  • The parser stops the header at the first non-comment line — don't put local declarations before closing the header block.
  • @detail is scoped to the group it follows — a new @group or @section clears the accumulated detail. Write all @detail lines before any control-map lines for that group.

docs.title: Plan (2026-10-26)
docs.text:
Work through the steps in order: fix what's broken first, document once behavior is stable, add features last. Each step points to the notes further down in this file.

Context for a new session - Engine: engine/lua-loader.js registers the Lua globals and the metro table; engine/grid-api.js holds the grid, MIDI, synth and metro timing. index.html holds the UI (script dropdown, MIDI monitor, FX). - iii reference: the firmware repo at ../neotrellis-monome has the real API. neotrellis_monome_picosdk_iii/src/iii/lua/lib.lua (metro, midi helpers, pset), src/iii/vm.c (built-ins such as midi_tx, fs_*), src/device_lua.c (grid functions). Match those when adding to the emulator. - Testing without a browser: run the real engine in node with the fengari npm package. Set globalThis.window = { fengari: require('fengari') } and a localStorage stub, import grid-api.js and lua-loader.js, override api.midi_note_on/off to count notes, call loader._execute(source, name), then drive keys with api._luaEventGrid(x, y, z) on timers. Run all scripts in scripts/manifest.json after engine changes to catch regressions. Confirm sound changes in the dev server (npm start). - External scripts can be fetched with gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<file>.lua --jq .content | base64 -d.

docs.title: Step 2 — Sound glitches
docs.text: Done in grid-api.js (2026-10-26), checked with a mocked Web Audio in node; confirm by ear in the dev server. - [x] Short fade on play/pause to remove clicks. The speaker toggle and volume fade (~60 ms) instead of jumping. Sound now really starts muted, as the speaker icon shows; clicking the grid or the speaker unmutes. - [x] Smooth delay-time changes (no crackles). A tape-style glide still crackled, so each time change now starts a new delay line (at most every 80 ms while dragging): new sound goes to it while the old line's echoes ring out (≤ 3 s). Delay amount and feedback ramp. - [x] Smooth reverb setting changes. Amount ramps. Decay applies on slider release: new sound goes to a new reverb while the old tail rings out. Decay 0 no longer throws.

docs.title: Step 5 — New sound features
docs.text:
• [x] Drum sounds (2026-10-26): engine/drums.js, seven drums ported from the Mangler (WAV.builder). General MIDI notes on one channel (36–51 = 4×4 pads), or a channel per drum; ⚄ re-rolls a drum; closed hat chokes open hat. In a new Sound tab.
  • [x] Sound tab pops out into a movable, resizable window (desktop); docked on mobile.
  • [x] Synth models (engine/synth.js): Triangle, Sine, Soft saw, Hollow square, Wide pad, Pluck, FM bell, with Drift (pitch wander) and Movement (filter sweep). Loudness matched (RMS 0.54–0.58).
  • [x] One place for sound (2026-10-26): the sound module under the grid is now volume, mute and ⚙ Sound; everything else is in the Sound tab (or its window). Engine in engine/sound.js.
  • [x] Several synths at once, each a tab with its own channel, preset (built-in or saved), model, envelope, drift, movement, filter (+ CC), level and sends to reverb, delay and chorus. The drum kit has level and sends too.
  • [x] Envelope editor: drag the points.
  • [x] Karplus–Strong strings (String, Nylon): computed per note into a buffer (a DelayNode feedback loop can't go above ~375 Hz); in tune within 0.4 cents from 82 to 1760 Hz.
  • [x] Chorus; reverb types Large room / hall and Plate / spring.
  • [x] Quality: Auto / Full / Light (light on phones: 6 voices per synth, short mono reverb, no chorus, no drift or movement).
  • [ ] Listen to all of it in the dev server: drum levels against the synths, the models and presets, both reverbs, the chorus.
  • [x] Long notes: the stuck-note guard is a setting (3 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, never; 30 s to start with), and ■ next to the volume stops everything (All Sound Off + All Notes Off on all 16 channels, and the emulator's sound).

docs.title: Open compatibility issues (found 2026-10-25)
docs.text:
Settled in Step 1; what's left for script writers is on the Hardware vs. Emulator page.

  • Firmware bug (for the firmware fork): lib.lua's slew.deinit() calls metro.free(slew.id), but slew.id is the metro, not its number, so it throws on the device and in the emulator. Fix: metro.free(slew.id.id), or store the number.
  • sluiiice calls metro.free(strumclock) with the metro; worth reporting to its author (see its note above).

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: The emulator's screen, part by part. To get it running, see Getting started.

docs.title: Loading a script
docs.text:
The script list at the top has these groups:

  • Recent: scripts you imported or opened, and scripts you edited, kept in this browser. ✕ Clear recent empties it.
  • Music, Colour demos, Tests, Write your own: the scripts that come with the emulator.
  • External scripts: scripts by other people, loaded from their own repositories each time.
  • tehn: scripts from monome's iii-scripts.

Pick one and press ▶ Load. Other ways to load a script:

  • Open File: a .lua file from your computer.
  • ⇱ Import script repo: paste a GitHub or Codeberg address, such as github.com/owner/repo or owner/repo. The emulator finds the .lua file and the README.

The other buttons:

  • ↻ Reload (or R) starts the script again.
  • ↓ Source downloads a bundled script as it is.
  • ↓ Device downloads a copy without comments, ready to upload, and warns about code the device won't load (see Hardware vs. emulator).

The status bar next to them shows what's happening, including errors and warnings. Scripts can set their grid size and rotation; the emulator switches to it when they load.

docs.title: The grid
docs.text:
• Click a pad to press it.
  • Right-click holds a pad down; right-click again to let go. Use it for chords, or for a button you'd otherwise hold.
  • Grid sets the size (8×8, 16×8, 8×16, 16×16), ↻ 0° rotates it, and the zoom slider and ⤢ Fit set how big it is on screen.
  • Full View shows only the grid. Its buttons open the sound and zoom controls; Esc leaves.
  • ◐ View sets the theme (dark or light; in light, unlit pads have a fine texture and lit ones are smooth, so even dim white LEDs stand out), the keys (NeoTrellis: the whole pad lights up; Mechatrellis: dark keys close together, with an LED at the top), the pad corners (square, slightly round, round), and the grid: Colour like a NeoTrellis grid, or Monochrome like a monome grid. In monochrome the script doesn't get grid_led_rgb, grid_color and grid_color_intensity, so it runs its own fallback; the grid label says "mono".

The line under the grid shows the script's own keyboard shortcuts, if it lists any.

docs.title: Scripts with more than one screen
docs.text:
Some scripts draw more than one screen, such as a main screen and a settings page.

  • Small thumbnails of each screen sit under the grid. Click one to show that screen.
  • ⊞ Dual View shows a second screen next to the main grid.

See multiple screens for how a script does this.

docs.title: Live Manual
docs.text: The Live Manual switch draws the script's controls over the grid: labels with lines to the pads they belong to. The labels come from comments in the script (see the script standard). A panel with the script's guide opens next to it.

docs.title: The side panel
docs.text:
Tab Shows Docs The script's name, version and author, and its controls, read from the comments in the script Guide The script's README State The starting values of simple variables in the script Source The script's code, coloured, with line numbers; see below Console Everything the status bar showed. The script's own print output goes to the browser's developer console (F12) MIDI Every MIDI message going in and out; see below Sound The synth's sound and the drum kit; see Sound

Drag the edge of the panel to make it wider.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
• Wrap wraps long lines. When a Lua error names a line, that line is marked, and the link at the top jumps to it.
  • ✎ Edit opens the code in an editor. ▶ Run (or Ctrl+Enter) runs your version. Auto-run runs it again a second after you stop typing.
  • Lines you changed are flagged: amber for changed, green for added, a red tick where lines were removed. Click a flag to put that part back, or ↺ Restore all. Ctrl+Z undoes a restore.
  • Your edited version is kept under Recent. It isn't saved to a file: use ↓ Device or copy it out.

docs.title: MIDI monitor
docs.text: The buttons at the top filter what's shown: notes, CC, clock, other messages, incoming, outgoing. ⏸ Pause stops capturing (the list and the counters at the bottom) and ⌫ Clear empties it.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text:
The emulator plays every note the script sends: drum notes on the drum kit, the others on the synths. Under the grid are the volume, the speaker button, ■ and ⚙ Sound, which opens the Sound tab (or, in Full View, the Sound window). Sound starts muted; the first click on the grid turns it on.

■ stops every note at once: it sends All Sound Off and All Notes Off on all 16 MIDI channels, so your MIDI devices stop too, and stops the emulator's own sound.

The sound also plays when a MIDI output is selected. Mute it to hear only your own synth.

docs.title: The Sound tab
docs.text:
Along the top: a tab for each synth, Drums, + to add a synth, and Effects.

A synth plays the notes on its channel (or on any channel) that the drum kit doesn't take. Synths on the same channel play together, so two can be layered.

  • Name and channel, ▶ Try to hear it, ✕ to remove it.
  • Preset: a starting point (Soft keys, Warm pad, Glass bell, Pluck, Drifting lead, Plucked string, Hollow bass), or one you saved with Save as… (kept in this browser).
  • Sound: Triangle, Sine, Soft saw, Hollow square, Wide pad, Pluck, FM bell, or a plucked string: String (bright, long) or Nylon (darker, shorter). The strings are Karplus–Strong: every note starts from a fresh burst of noise in a delay line tuned to the note, so no two plucks sound the same; harder notes (higher velocity) sound brighter.
  • Envelope: drag the points. The first sets the attack, the second the decay and sustain level, the line after it the sustain level, the last the release.
  • Drift puts each note a little out of tune and lets it wander slowly; Movement sweeps each note's filter slowly.
  • Filter: a low-pass filter, which also follows a CC (74 to start with) on the synth's channel, from the script or from MIDI in.
  • Level, and how much it sends to the reverb, delay and chorus.

Drums: seven drums (kick, snare, closed and open hat, clap, tom, perc), made by the emulator rather than recorded.

  • Plays drum notes on channel …: notes on that channel (10 to start with, or any) play drums by their General MIDI number: 36 kick, 38 snare, 39 clap, 42 closed hat, 46 open hat, and so on. Notes 36 to 51, the usual 4×4 pad layout, are all covered. Other notes go to the synths.
  • Plays a channel per drum: each drum plays on any note on its own channel (10 to 16 to start with).
  • ▶ plays a drum, and flashes whenever the script plays it. ⚄ makes a new version of that drum; ⚄ All does all of them.
  • The closed hat cuts off the open hat, as on a real kit. The kit has its own level and effect sends.

A script such as iiinvert sends its drums on channel 1: set the kit to channel 1 to hear them as drums.

Effects, shared by all synths and the kit:

  • Reverb: Large room / hall (a short gap, then a tail that darkens) or Plate / spring (bright and dense straight away). A new decay applies when you let go of the slider.
  • Delay: time and feedback.
  • Chorus: rate and depth.
  • Quality: Light plays fewer notes at once and has a shorter reverb, no chorus and no drift or movement, for phones. Auto picks light on phones.
  • Stuck notes: a note the script never ends stops by itself after 30 s, or the time you pick (3 s to 1 min, or never).

⧉ Pop out moves the Sound controls into a window of their own, which you can drag by its title and resize from its corner; Dock puts them back. Everything in the Sound tab is kept in this browser.

docs.title: MIDI
docs.text:
Pick a MIDI In and MIDI Out at the top (Chrome or Edge); ↻ looks for new devices. The first time, the browser asks whether the page may use MIDI devices: allow it, or the lists stay empty.

The lists show the MIDI devices your computer knows. To reach a DAW or another program on the same computer, most systems need a virtual MIDI port; how to make one depends on your system.

  • Out sends the script's notes, CCs and clock.
  • In goes to the script's event_midi, for scripts that follow an external clock or a keyboard. For a script without event_midi, incoming notes press pads instead.

If the same device is both input and output, a script can hear its own messages; the status bar warns when that happens.

Timing. The emulator keeps tempo, but each note or clock tick can be a few milliseconds early or late, and more when the tab is in the background. That's fine for playing along; for tight sync with other gear, let the script follow an external clock (MIDI In), or run it on the grid. More in Hardware vs. emulator.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
R always reloads the script. The line under the grid shows what the other keys do in the loaded script.

A script can handle keys itself, with event_key (see the script standard). Sandman and LeaveSeqr do: Tab moves to their next screen. For a script without event_key, these keys press fixed pads:

Key Presses Tab x1, y8, while the key is down Space x1, y8 ↑ ← ↓ → x15 y7, x14 y8, x15 y8, x16 y8 1, 2, 3, 4 x10–x13, y3 A x1, y3

These match Serpentine's layout (ALT, the D-pad, tempo, autopilot). Keys don't reach the grid while you type in a text field, or with Ctrl or Cmd held.

docs.title: Kept in your browser
docs.text:
The emulator remembers, in this browser only:

  • the Recent list, including edited scripts
  • presets that scripts save with pset_write
  • the Source tab's Wrap and Auto-run settings
  • the theme, keys, pad corners and grid mode from ◐ View
  • the synths, drum kit, effects and quality settings, your saved presets, and where the Sound window was

Clearing the site's data in your browser removes them.
